## Left open by the earlier read (RD-047)

An independent reader judged the previous rewrite of this lesson. Fix everything below as well. Each item is as serious as an item under "Fix these".

### Findings

1. Rule L02 (Major). Problem: The sentence stacks several technical offense relationships. The explanation of frustrated offense that follows does not explain necessarily included offenses. A Grade 5 reader cannot readily apply this part of the rule.
   > It also covers an attempt, a frustrated form of the offense, or an offense that necessarily includes or is included in the first charge.
2. Rule L25 (Major). Problem: The learner needs the meaning of an offense necessarily including another to use this rule. No explanation, concrete illustration, prerequisite reference, or later signpost supplies it. Defining frustrated offense does not explain this separate relationship.
   > It also covers an attempt, a frustrated form of the offense, or an offense that necessarily includes or is included in the first charge.

## Left open by the earlier read (RD-048)

An independent reader judged the previous rewrite of this lesson. Fix everything below as well. Each item is as serious as an item under "Fix these".

### Findings

1. Rule B01 (Blocker). Problem: The preceding sentence applies this procedure to both search and arrest warrants. For arrest warrants, personal determination of probable cause does not require the judge personally to examine complainants or witnesses; evaluation of the prosecutor’s report and supporting records can suffice. This conflates the procedures. Source basis: Article III Section 2 read with the settled distinction in Soliven v. Makasiar; no external source was opened under the prompt-only restriction.
   > The judge must decide this personally after examining the complainant and any witnesses under an oath or affirmation, a formal promise to tell the truth.
2. Rule L27 (Major). Problem: The lesson teaches applying search and seizure rules but names no warrantless-search or warrantless-arrest condition. Saying exceptions exist does not tell students when they apply. No prerequisite or later explanation is identified for those exceptions.
   > Some searches and arrests are lawful without a warrant, so a missing warrant alone does not settle every case.
